claims.statement: The async get_agent(config) factory in agent/server.py compiles the primary coding agent per executable thread run by resolving its sandbox, model policy, tool surface, subagent, skills, and middleware before calling create_deep_agent.

get_agent returns a bare create_deep_agent with empty system prompt and no tools, sandbox, or supplied middleware when there is no thread_id or the load is not for execution, gated by graph_loaded_for_execution reading the __is_for_execution__ configurable flag.

get_agent starts a cached SandboxBackendProxy for the thread with a reconnect callback that builds a LocalShellBackend for desktop runs and otherwise calls ensure_sandbox_for_thread with the selected workspace.

The main and subagent model settings resolve in get_agent by precedence: workspace defaults, dashboard profile overrides, stored thread settings, then an explicit per-run agent_model_id and agent_effort validated against SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS and model_supports_effort.

construct_system_prompt renders the ordered per-thread main-agent template with working, source, plan, repository, workspace, and optional admin guidance, while render_open_swe_shared_base appends the static OPEN_SWE_SHARED_BASE with conditional sandbox-download guidance.

The CompositeBackend overlays bundled skills from a read-only FilesystemBackend, hosted organization and credential-verified user skills from read-only StoreBackends namespaced in the LangGraph store, and desktop user skills from a read-only StateBackend; its ordered skill_sources list is shared with the general-purpose subagent.

The configured general-purpose subagent compiles independently of parent middleware, so it carries its own dynamic-tool and exclusion middleware, workflow-push guard, and model guards including SanitizeOpenAIResponsesMiddleware and ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware.

The main agent's middleware list starts with conversation offloading and preparation and ends with ModelCallTimeoutMiddleware, so the model-call deadline covers the provider call and a timeout escalates outward to the fallback model.

PlanModeMiddleware is installed unconditionally with the factory's initial configurable plan_mode value, resets state to that value at run start, and filters each model request so a mid-run enter_plan_mode command restricts the next turn without leaking stale plan mode into a later run.

PrepareAgentRunMiddleware appends sender identity, attribution, user instructions, and participant context as a separate generated context message after a human input, deduplicating already-visible dynamic context rather than placing participant input in the per-thread system prompt.

ensure_sandbox_for_thread does not replace an unreachable existing sandbox by default because that may lose uncommitted work, but it replaces a deleted sandbox so the thread is not permanently bound to a stale id.

The graph is registered as agent.graphs.agent:traced_agent, which re-exports get_agent, and get_agent binds its result with a config stripped of __pregel_* runtime internals to avoid serializing a read-time runtime into later calls.

RunConfig treats configurable as a tolerant cross-launcher contract: declared fields are optional, unknown keys are retained, and parsing removes invalid fields individually rather than discarding the rest of the configuration.

Hosted assembly persists the resolved main/subagent settings and repository instructions before applying the Fable availability gate; model construction failures become deferred error models, and fallback middleware is installed only for a different model id.

BasePrepareRunMiddleware checkpoints per-run setup with a fingerprint of middleware type, latest message, and configuration; retries before checkpoint persistence require preparation to be idempotent, while later invocations re-prepare fresh context.

Desktop runs route Deep Agents' virtual /large_tool_results/ and /conversation_history directories to a thread-specific artifact root outside the selected repository so offloads do not become git changes.

DynamicToolMiddleware clears loaded integration selections at each run start, requires load_integration_tools before an integration tool call, serializes each group's construction, converts failures into unavailable-tool results, and rejects collisions with reserved names.

When plan mode is active, its exclusion set removes task delegation and selected external mutation, but leaves file editing and execute available; excluding task prevents delegation to an independently compiled subagent from bypassing the parent restriction.

The parent static tool surface is conditional: trusted Slack context enables Slack tools, authorized admin threads add ADMIN_TOOLS, desktop and stop-summary runs use restricted lists, and ExcludeToolsMiddleware applies normal or stop-summary Deep Agent exclusions.

Focused assembly tests cover the backend and skills routes, desktop and stop-summary tool surfaces, parent-only subagent boundaries, guards, and middleware order; dedicated tests also check concurrent eager tool loading and profile/subagent model behavior.

Workspace MCP and Notion integration tools are loaded concurrently during assembly only when a hosted non-stop-summary run has a known credential scope, then exposed through DynamicToolMiddleware rather than the static tool list.

When adaptive model routing is enabled, get_agent constructs fast, balanced, and performance route models, records routing metadata, and installs ModelSelectionMiddleware; a Slack ask run instead forces the fast route and disables adaptive routing for that run.

For hosted runs whose credential scope is unknown, get_agent omits personal tools and MCP loading and installs WorkspaceSkillsMiddleware so organization/workspace skills remain available without granting that personal integration surface.
